description:
Test-strategy review of the UAT harness (`tests/uat/`) found four
independent ways the accounting can overstate corpus coverage or hide
failures - none of them are individually catastrophic, but together they
mean the "total_defined" denominator and the report exit code cannot be
trusted at face value:

(a) `tests/uat/phases/enumerate.py:94-95` - `enumerate_cells_with_pruning`
    iterates `benchmark_list` and does `info = benchmarks.get(benchmark);
    if info is None: continue` for benchmarks named in the config that
    are absent from the registry. This is a silent drop: no
    `CompatibilityPrunedCell` row, no log line, no accounting entry at
    all - the benchmark simply vanishes from both `cells` and
    `compatibility_pruned`, and downstream `total_defined_count`
    (report.py:165, `attempted + skipped + unreachable`) never knew it
    was supposed to exist. A typo'd benchmark name in a sweep config
    fails this way with zero signal.

(b) `tests/uat/matrix.py:302-319` (`filter_scales_by_registry`) drops
    requested scales that fall outside a benchmark's declared
    `scale_options` ("ladder pruning"). Confirmed via
    `tests/uat/phases/enumerate.py:108-111`: the filtered-out scales are
    just absent from `filtered` - there is no equivalent of
    `compatibility_pruned` for registry/ladder-based drops. Only
    compatibility-RULE prunes (platform/benchmark incompatibility) get an
    accounting row; ladder prunes (scale outside registry bounds) get
    none. `tests/uat/phases/report.py` has no ladder-pruned counter
    field/parameter at all, so this class of denominator shrinkage cannot
    even be reported if a caller wanted to.

(c) Regenerating a report from a `cells.jsonl` whose sidecar
    `cells.jsonl.accounting.json` is missing silently reports
    `unreachable=0` and drops the `release_gate_attention` flag. This
    is DELIBERATE and already pinned by
    `tests/uat/test_report_accounting.py:116-143`
    (`test_report_cli_without_sidecar_defaults_unreachable_zero`,
    docstring: "Older artifacts predate the sidecar; the report must
    still regenerate.") - flagged here as a real gap worth revisiting,
    not a bug to fix outright: silently defaulting to 0 for OLDER
    artifacts trades one risk (crashing on legitimate legacy re-runs)
    for another (a report that looks clean when unreachable-ness was
    simply never computed). Decide in w1 whether the harness should
    instead surface a visible "sidecar missing, unreachable count
    unknown" marker distinct from "sidecar present, unreachable=0" for
    genuinely clean runs.

(d) `tests/uat/phases/report.py:54-57` -
    `ReportSummary.exit_code()` returns `2` if aborted, else `1` only
    if `cross_scale_floor_breached` (an OPT-IN check - `cross_scale_floor`
    defaults to `None` at report.py:51/142 and is only enforced when a
    caller explicitly passes it), else `0`. This means a report full of
    `fail`/`timeout`/`unreachable` cells still exits `0` unless the
    caller happens to have opted into the cross-scale floor check - CI
    or a human eyeballing an exit code alone would see "success" for a
    corpus that mostly failed.

anti_patterns.dont: invent a second, differently-shaped accounting file format for ladder-pruned or registry-absent cells
anti_patterns.why: compatibility_pruned.jsonl already exists and downstream tooling (matrix_summary.tsv rendering) expects one pruned-accounting shape

anti_patterns.dont: make --strict (if chosen in w1) the implicit default for existing Makefile/CI callers without checking whether any of them rely on today's lenient exit code
anti_patterns.why: that would silently turn a previously-green UAT pipeline red

anti_patterns.dont: silently change tests/uat/test_report_accounting.py's pinned unreachable=0-without-sidecar assertion in w5
anti_patterns.instead: add a new field instead of changing the existing default.
anti_patterns.why: that test intentionally documents backward-compat behavior for older artifacts per its own docstring

preserves.behavior: All existing compatibility-rule pruning behavior and CompatibilityPrunedCell accounting rows continue to work unchanged - w2/w3 add coverage, they don't replace the existing mechanism.

tests/uat/cli.py's existing report/enumerate subcommand argument surface stays backward compatible - if w1 picks the --strict-flag option, it must be additive (default off) unless explicitly decided otherwise.

tests/uat/test_report_accounting.py:116-143 (test_report_cli_without_sidecar_defaults_unreachable_zero) - the pinned unreachable=0-without-sidecar behavior for legacy artifact regeneration must not silently break; w5 adds visibility, it does not remove the default.

work_units.notes:
Two options, pick one and document the decision inline in
report.py's module docstring:
  1. Change `ReportSummary.exit_code()` default behavior so any
     `fail_count > 0 or timeout_count > 0 or unreachable_count > 0`
     returns non-zero (e.g. `1`), independent of the opt-in
     cross_scale_floor check. This makes "report exit code == 0"
     mean "everything attempted actually passed."
  2. Keep today's lenient default (exit 0 unless cross-scale floor
     breached) but add an explicit `--strict` CLI flag to the report
     phase that opts into failing on any fail/timeout/unreachable
     count, for callers (e.g. release-gate automation) that want a
     hard gate.
Recommendation: prefer option 2 (additive `--strict` flag) if any
existing caller currently depends on today's lenient default (check
`tests/uat/cli.py` and any Makefile targets that call `uat report`
before deciding) - otherwise option 1 is the more honest default.
This decision blocks w4 (exit_code implementation/tests).

DECISION (2026-07-04): Option 1 (default-strict), no --strict flag.
Evidence gathered before deciding:
  - The UAT CLI file is actually `tests/uat/_cli.py` (the YAML's
    `tests/uat/cli.py` does not exist - naming drift; `_cli.py` is the
    argparse entry point `make uat-report` calls via
    `python -m tests.uat._cli report`). Its `_handle_report` prints
    the report's exit code straight through (`return summary.exit_code()`)
    with no branching, `|| true`, or exit-code interpretation.
  - `Makefile`'s `uat-report` target (~line 1983) just shells out to
    `python -m tests.uat._cli report ...`; it does not inspect or
    branch on the resulting exit code either.
  - Grepped `.github/workflows/` for `uat-report`/`uat report`/`_cli
    report`: no matches. No CI workflow parses or gates on this exit
    code today.
  - The UAT orchestrator (`tests/uat/orchestrator.py`, out of scope)
    already folds the report phase's `exit_code()` into
    `SweepResult.exit_code()` via `max(phase_exit_codes.values())`; no
    orchestrator or e2e test (`test_orchestrator.py`,
    `test_e2e_integration.py`) asserts `exit_code() == 0` for a run
    containing an actual fail/timeout/unreachable cell outside of the
    aborted/cross-scale-floor-breached cases that already return
    nonzero.
  - The only place that DID rely on the old lenient default was this
    TODO's own test suite: `tests/uat/test_report_accounting.py`'s
    `test_report_cli_reconciles_skipped_and_unreachable_fixture`
    (fixture has a failed + an unreachable cell) and
    `test_report_cli_reads_skipped_unreachable_sidecar` (sidecar
    reports 3 unreachable) both asserted `exit_code == 0` - updated to
    `exit_code == 1` as part of w4, per the anti-pattern's own carve-out
    for updating tests, not because anything outside the test suite
    depended on the leniency.
Conclusion: no real caller depends on "exit 0 despite failures," so
option 1 (the more honest default) was chosen over the additive
`--strict` flag. Full reasoning is duplicated in
`tests/uat/phases/report.py`'s module docstring.
work_units.summary: Decide (d) exit-code policy: non-zero exit on failures by default, or an explicit --strict flag

work_units.notes:
In `enumerate_cells_with_pruning` (tests/uat/phases/enumerate.py:94-95),
replace the bare `continue` with an accounting entry. Reuse the
existing `CompatibilityPrunedCell` shape if it fits (e.g. a
synthetic `rule_id="benchmark-not-in-registry"`), or add a small
sibling record type if `CompatibilityPrunedCell`'s fields don't
naturally fit a benchmark-level (not platform+benchmark-pair) drop.
Either way, the config-benchmark-not-in-registry case must show up
somewhere in `EnumerationResult` so it's visible in accounting output
and can be surfaced in the report, not just silently absent.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: investigation found the real silent drop happens
one layer earlier than the cited line. `resolve_benchmarks`
(tests/uat/matrix.py) already filters `benchmarks.include` down to
`bid in benchmarks` before returning `benchmark_list`, so
`enumerate_cells_with_pruning`'s `info = benchmarks.get(benchmark);
if info is None` can never actually fire for a typo'd `include` entry
in current code - `benchmark_list` never contains an id absent from
`benchmarks` to begin with. Fixed at the true source: added
`matrix.missing_benchmarks_from_include(include, benchmarks)` (new,
tested function) to expose exactly which `include` ids `resolve_benchmarks`
silently dropped; `enumerate_cells_with_pruning` now calls it and emits
one `CompatibilityPrunedCell` row per platform x requested scale with
`rule_id="benchmark-not-in-registry"`, `status="pruned-registry"` (kept
the original `if info is None` line too, now also building the same
kind of row, as a defensive no-op in case a future caller passes a
`benchmark_list`/`benchmarks` pair that diverges). Reused
`CompatibilityPrunedCell` as-is (no sibling type needed) - the
platform+benchmark+scale shape fits fine when applied once per
platform for a benchmark-level drop.
work_units.summary: (a) Record registry-absent benchmarks as an accounting row instead of a silent continue

work_units.notes:
`filter_scales_by_registry` (tests/uat/matrix.py:302-319) currently
only returns the surviving scales. Change the call site in
`enumerate_cells_with_pruning` (tests/uat/phases/enumerate.py:108-111)
to also capture the DROPPED scales (`set(requested) - set(filtered)`)
and record them as accounting rows (reuse or extend the same
structure introduced in w2 if appropriate - a "pruned" superset
covering both compatibility-rule and ladder-registry reasons keeps
report.py's counting logic simpler than two parallel lists).
Add a `ladder_pruned_count` (or a unified `registry_pruned_count`)
field to `ReportSummary` and thread it through
`total_defined_count`'s computation (report.py:165) so pruned-by-
ladder cells count toward the true denominator instead of vanishing.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: `enumerate_cells_with_pruning` now computes
`dropped = [s for s in requested if s not in filtered]` at the call
site and emits one `CompatibilityPrunedCell` per dropped scale
(`rule_id=f"uat.ladder.{benchmark}.scale-not-in-registry"`,
`status="pruned-registry"`) into the SAME `compatibility_pruned` list
as w2 and the existing compatibility-rule prunes - this means
`execute.py`/`orchestrator.py` (both out of scope, untouched) already
forward and count these rows for free via their existing
`len(execute_outcome.compatibility_pruned)` wiring, so real sweeps get
the denominator fix with zero changes to those files. Deliberately
SKIPPED emitting a row when the min_scale fallback
(`if not filtered and ... info.min_scale is not None: filtered =
[info.min_scale]`) substitutes a whole-ladder-invalid benchmark's
canonical scale (e.g. joinorder/tpcds_obt requested at the 0.01 smoke
scale but only valid at 1.0) - that path still produces an executed
cell with signal, it is a substitution not a silent drop, and treating
it as "pruned" broke `test_phases.py::
test_enumerate_keeps_release_gate_runtime_envelopes_for_diagnostic_sweeps`'s
`all(rule_id.endswith(".benchmark_gate"))` assertion for no real
accounting benefit. Also added `ReportSummary.registry_pruned_count`
(default 0) threaded into `skipped_count`/`total_defined_count` in
`report.py`, plus a `registry_pruned=N` field in both TSV footer
lines. Known limitation, documented rather than worked around: since
`orchestrator.py` is out of scope, it still only passes
`compatibility_pruned_count=len(execute_outcome.compatibility_pruned)`
(which now already includes the w2/w3 rows) and never populates the
new, separate `registry_pruned_count` parameter - so for real sweeps
the denominator is already correct via the shared bucket, but the
granular "how many were registry/ladder vs. compatibility-rule"
breakdown in the report needs a follow-up orchestrator.py change to
populate `registry_pruned_count` from a filtered subset of
`compatibility_pruned` (e.g. by `status == "pruned-registry"`) to be
visible end-to-end.
work_units.summary: (b) Add ladder-pruned accounting: record registry-filtered scales and thread through report.py

work_units.notes:
This is the most delicate change since
`tests/uat/test_report_accounting.py:116-143` currently PINS
`unreachable == 0` with no sidecar as intended behavior for
"older artifacts." Do not silently change that pinned test's
expected value. Instead, add a way to distinguish "sidecar present,
confirmed unreachable=0" from "sidecar absent, unreachable
unknown/assumed 0" - e.g. a new `unreachable_count_is_estimated: bool`
field on `ReportSummary`, surfaced in both the JSON payload
(`payload["unreachable_is_estimated"]`) and the TSV comment line
(alongside the existing `# UNREACHABLE_CELLS=N release_gate_attention=...`
comment at report.py:194). Update
`test_report_cli_without_sidecar_defaults_unreachable_zero` to also
assert the new estimated flag is `True`, and add a companion
assertion to the WITH-sidecar test that it's `False`. This is
additive (keeps the pinned default-zero behavior) rather than a
breaking change to the existing contract.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: `ReportSummary.unreachable_count_is_estimated`
(default False) added and threaded through `write_report()`'s new
`unreachable_count_is_estimated` parameter. The sidecar-presence
signal has to originate in `tests/uat/_cli.py` (report.py's
`write_report()` only ever sees an already-resolved int, it has no
way to know whether that int came from a real sidecar) - so
`_read_skipped_unreachable_sidecar` was changed from returning just
`int` to returning `tuple[int, bool]` (count, sidecar_present), and
`_handle_report` passes `unreachable_count_is_estimated=not
sidecar_present` into `write_report()` and adds
`"unreachable_is_estimated"` to the printed JSON payload. The TSV
`# UNREACHABLE_CELLS=...` line's guard changed from `if
unreachable_count:` to `if unreachable_count or
unreachable_count_is_estimated:` so the line now also appears (with
`release_gate_attention=not_required unreachable_is_estimated=true`)
for the confirmed-zero-but-estimated case, which previously printed no
line at all; the confirmed-zero-and-not-estimated case is unchanged
(still prints nothing). Pinned test
`test_report_cli_without_sidecar_defaults_unreachable_zero` keeps its
`exit_code == 0` and `unreachable == 0` assertions unchanged, only
gaining the new `unreachable_is_estimated is True` assertion per the
instructions; the WITH-sidecar test
(`test_report_cli_reads_skipped_unreachable_sidecar`) gained the
companion `unreachable_is_estimated is False` assertion.
work_units.summary: (c) Revisit sidecar-missing default: add a visible unreachable-unknown marker
